Hi Ellen / Sage team —

Thanks for confirming the kickoff window. To keep the first two weeks focused and measurable I've put together a short "burnup" view of onboarding work (attached) and a proposed owners list for observability topics: dashboards, tracing hooks, error taxonomy, alert routing and runbooks.

Quick asks for this thread:
- Can you confirm the internal on-call email and PagerDuty team name we should route alerts to?
- Please review the attachment (Sage_Onboarding_MAP.xlsx) and mark any items you want to reprioritize.
- Assign an internal SME from your side for tracing instrumentation (we'll need sample traces).

Proposed Redwood owners:
- Dashboards & SLOs: Marissa Cole
- Tracing hooks & instrumentation details: Aditya Rao
- Error taxonomy & runbook drafts: Grace O'Connor

I've attached a runbook template (runbook-template.md) so we can align on the format for incident playbooks. We'll finalize owners and a first pass on the runbook by end of week.

Thanks — look forward to getting this into motion.

— Jonas

Jonas — thanks, this is helpful. A couple things from our side:
- On-call routing: route-critical@sageops.io and our PagerDuty team is "Sage - Platform Ops" (PD: https://sage.pagerduty.com/team/platops).
- Tracing SME: I'll loop in our lead platform engineer, Miguel, separately with sample trace spans; he prefers to send a small consolidated JSON sample rather than access to the system.
- Timeline: we can commit to the first runbook draft by 5/19.

Two questions:
1) For alert routing, can Redwood support a dual-path (email + PD) for P0 only? We want PD for true incidents and email for P1/P2 until we complete our PD tuning.
2) Do you have suggested latency thresholds for our initial SLOs? We're instrumenting two inference routes: text-generation-standard and embeddings-batch.

Thanks — Ellen

Thanks Ellen — confirmed routing details. To address both questions:
- Dual-path routing: yes, we can create an alert policy that sends P0 to PD and P1/P2 to email. We'll draft the exact routing rules and share a short matrix (P0/P1/P2 definitions + destination).
- Initial latency thresholds (proposal):
  * text-generation-standard: p50 < 250ms, p95 < 600ms, p99 < 1.3s
  * embeddings-batch: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 400ms (batch size dependent)

Owners & immediate next steps:
- Marissa (me): dashboard templates & SLO dashboard (deliver by 5/18)
- Aditya: tracing hooks sample + instrumentation notes (deliver by 5/17)
- Grace: error taxonomy draft & runbook first pass (deliver by 5/19)

I'll attach a short routing matrix as a follow-up; if that looks good we'll create the initial alert policies in your account and run an in-situ test.

— Marissa

Date: 2028-05-17T11:07:00-07:00
Subject: Tracing hooks & instrumentation notes — text-generation-standard / embeddings-batch

Ellen / team — attached are minimal tracing guidelines that match Redwood's runtime hooks. Key points:
- Span model: top-level span = inference_request (tags: request_id, customer_id, model, endpoint, sequence_length)
- Child spans: tokenize -> model_infer -> kv_cache_lookup -> response_serialize
- Sample event for request_id 0a1b2c: {"request_id":"0a1b2c","model":"rw-v2-1-xl","seq_len":128,"p50_ms":210} (we agreed only metadata is shared).

Alerting knobs to wire into traces/metrics:
- p95_latency_ms > 600 => trigger P1 (email)
- p99_latency_ms > 1.25s => trigger P0 (PD)
- error_rate_5m > 0.5% on text-generation-standard => P0 if sustained > 5 minutes

Instrumenting tips: add a trace_id header propagation (X-Trace-Id) and ensure the request_id maps to your internal trace. We can provide a small middleware snippet for Go/Node if helpful.

I'll upload the sample traces to the Drive folder and include a short code snippet in the runbook template.

— Aditya
Aditya Rao
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
